subject: EdgeHealth pilot — residency (TIA) & UK addendum scoping
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@edgehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T16:12:00Z
Subject: Pilot data residency + TIA scope questions

Hi Jonas (and Marissa),

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As we scoped the pilot we surfaced two items the legal/compliance team needs to confirm before we can move to procurement: a precise TIA/DTIA scoping statement for the EU pilot and the status of Redwood's UK addendum (IDTA) support. Specifically:

- Will Redwood be able to provide a documented TIA scope that limits processing to EU-hosted inference and describes subprocessor paths? We need the scope to present to our DPO.
- Do you have a UK IDTA or equivalent addendum that covers your subprocessor list and any onshore caching fallback behavior? Our UK team requires the addendum text or an express mapping to SCCs.
- A short list of the subprocessors that will touch cleartext at any point for the pilot (not just compute providers) and whether any are in jurisdictions outside the EEA/UK.

I've attached a brief template that our privacy team prefers for scoping (EdgeHealth_TIA_scope.xlsx). We can accept redacted technical diagrams if helpful.

If you can share a draft DPA addendum or point us to the signed template and a subprocessor map, that would speed procurement. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call later this week.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
EdgeHealth Inc.
[Attachment: EdgeHealth_TIA_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T18:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Pilot data residency + TIA scope questions

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding EdgeHealth's ask above. High priority pilot (sales motion live) and they're asking for:

1) A TIA scope statement that we can commit to for the pilot (EU inference only, onshore logging controls, KV cache residency).
2) UK addendum / IDTA status + whether we have a UK-specific addendum that includes subprocessor mapping and fallback descriptions.
3) Subprocessor list that may touch cleartext; they want jurisdiction info.

Notes from the demo ops team: pilot will use our hosted EU region with cache fallbacks if latency spikes; some cached context may be written to ephemeral storage in a US-based analytics pipeline unless we block it. We should consider whether we can promise no analytics export for the pilot.

I attached our current subprocessor map and a draft DPA addendum we sometimes use for UK inquiries (redwood-subprocessor-map-202803.pdf, dpa-uk-addendum-draft.docx).

Proposed next steps: Kimberly to confirm whether the dpa-uk-addendum-draft is acceptable to hold as an interim addendum and list the exact subprocessors that touch cleartext. Marissa to confirm ops constraints (can we disable analytics export for the pilot?). If both green, I'll reply to Samantha with the scope + attachments and propose a doc-sign cadence.

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Trust & Policy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-subprocessor-map-202803.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T09:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot data residency + TIA scope questions

Thanks Jonas. Quick answers and redlines below — I also drafted a short TIA scope paragraph you can share with EdgeHealth.

- DPA/UK addendum: The dpa-uk-addendum-draft.docx is our standard UK addendum language for hosted customers. It maps to SCCs where required and includes a subprocessor appendix. For a pilot we can provide the draft under NDA and mark it as interim until procurement requests countersigned docs. We should not sign until legal has tracked the contract number, but we can share the draft text.

- Subprocessors & cleartext: Per the current map, the only subprocessors that may access cleartext logs are a) our managed logs provider for incidents (LogSafe EU node, Ireland) and b) a third-party analytics pipeline that currently runs in the US (MetricsFlow). However, MetricsFlow can be gated off — ops already confirmed we can disable analytics export for the pilot. We should document that as a contract warranty for the pilot window.

- TIA paragraph you can share (use exactly):
"Redwood will restrict processing for the EdgeHealth pilot to EU-hosted inference nodes (Frankfurt and Dublin) and will not route inference requests to non-EEA regions. KV cache and transient logs will remain within the EEA for the duration of the pilot. Persistent analytics exports to third-party pipelines will be disabled for this pilot unless otherwise agreed in writing; any temporary routing to US-based support tools will be limited to on-call debugging and subject to data minimization and access logs."

- Evidence asked by procurement: provide signed subprocessor attestations for LogSafe and a screenshot of the region routing table showing Frankfurt/Dublin nodes. Also provide the draft addendum doc and the TIA scope spreadsheet completed.

I'll add two small redlines to the dpa-uk-addendum-draft: explicit warranty that no persistent analytics export will be enabled during the pilot; and an evidence handoff schedule (14 days). Please advise if EdgeHealth wants a longer retention or rolling evidence windows.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dpa-uk-addendum-draft.docx]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T00:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot data residency + TIA scope questions

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the spreadsheet. Quick summary and what I attached for you:

1) TIA scope (attached): we confirm the pilot will be constrained to EU-hosted inference nodes (Frankfurt + Dublin). KV cache and transient logs will remain within the EEA for the pilot window.
2) UK addendum: attached is our draft UK addendum (interim, for review). Kimberly has proposed two redlines we suggest as contract language for the pilot (no persistent analytics export; 14-day evidence handoff).
3) Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor map. The only subprocessors with potential cleartext access are LogSafe (Ireland) and MetricsFlow (US). MetricsFlow will be disabled for the pilot; we will provide attestation from LogSafe.

Attachments included: EdgeHealth_TIA_scope.xlsx (completed), redwood-subprocessor-map-202803.pdf, dpa-uk-addendum-draft.docx.

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm acceptance of the TIA paragraph above and the two UK addendum redlines.
- If accepted, we'll provide the LogSafe attestation and the routing screenshot within 5 business days and circulate a DocuSign link for the interim addendum.
- If you prefer a different evidence cadence, tell us and we can adjust.

Would you like a 30-minute call Thursday 10:00 AM BST to walk the legal team through the TIA wording?

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Trust & Policy
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: EdgeHealth_TIA_scope.xlsx, redwood-subprocessor-map-202803.pdf, dpa-uk-addendum-draft.docx]
